title: Oxygène 3
label: Sony · Columbia
overview:
Released on the 40th anniversary of Oxygène to the day, this third and final chapter was composed in six weeks and mixed entirely in Ableton Live — a deliberate choice Jarre describes as maintaining the minimalist constraint of the 1976 original, where an 8-track studio enforced discipline. The instrument list deliberately mirrors the earlier albums — Eminent 310, EMS Synthi AKS, ARP 2500/2600, Mellotron — alongside modern additions including Moog Sub 37, Teenage Engineering OP-1, Elektron Analog Keys and digital VSTs. Jarre described a "light and dark" architecture: the album moves from introspection toward resolution across its seven parts.

Oxygène (Part 19) was the compositional genesis: a piece written during the Electronica 1 sessions that made Jarre reconsider what the series could be in 2016. Part 20 directly samples wind and white-noise material from the original Oxygène Part VI, closing the trilogy with an explicit sonic quotation of its own origin. Parts 14–20 complete a sequence begun forty years earlier. Metacritic score: 65/100. UK Albums: No. 41; Switzerland: No. 14.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 14)
tracks.role: Album role: Entry into the 40th-anniversary chapter — re-establishes the trilogy's sonic world through the inherited instrument palette before introducing the darker, more restrained character of the album's first half.

events.description: spare, familiar arpeggiation in the Oxygène register; the sonic handshake that connects three decades.
events.detail: The opening is almost archivally careful: the timbral match to the 1976 album is exact enough to feel like time has not passed.

events.description: the melancholic string-organ pad characteristic of the entire trilogy fills the harmonic space.
low-frequency rhythmic grounding, more felt than heard; anchors the composition without imposing percussive structure.
events.detail: The Sub 37 is the most contemporary element in this track; its presence is integrated rather than announced.

events.description: resonant filter opens on the lead sequence, brightening the harmonic register.
the filter closes, the bass withdraws; the track retreats to its original register.
events.detail: Structural arch mirroring the large-scale design of Part 20: everything comes back to where it started.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 15)
tracks.role: Album role: Expansive second piece — the album's most patient track; a long-form melodic statement in the lower register that establishes the "dark side" character fully before it migrates toward shade in Part 16.

events.description: the same atmospheric device that bookmarks the trilogy; ARP enters cautiously over it.
events.detail: The wind noise is not ambient padding; it is the trilogy's recurring atmospheric signature, present in all three albums.

events.section: Long-form melodic statement in lower register
events.description: a broad, unhurried phrase that does not want to resolve quickly. The track's entire purpose is to let this melody breathe.
Mellotron D4000 enters with string swells; the melody becomes embroidered rather than solo.
events.detail: The Mellotron D4000 is a digital Mellotron model; its character is softer than the M400 used on Oxygène 7–13 but retains the analog warmth.

events.description: harmonic shift into a minor mode deeper than the opening; the melodic material takes on an uncertain quality.
layers recede, the wind texture reasserts, and the track fades without formal closure.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 16)
tracks.role: Album role: Dark side centrepiece — the longest track and deepest point of the album's introspective arc; harmonic ambiguity never settles, reflecting the ecological anxiety Jarre cited as the album's conceptual underpinning.

events.description: unhurried, low-pitched arpeggiation with wide spacing between events; space as tension.
the instrument's distinctive portamento and timbral instability give the melody a slightly unstable, searching quality.
events.detail: The Synthi AKS is Jarre's most expressive instrument choice: its patch matrix means no two performances are identical.

events.description: suspended chords and unresolved modal fragments accumulate; the track's "ecological warning" is clearest here.
events.detail: Jarre described the artwork and music as "an ecological warning signal, dark and surreal." This is the compositional correlate.

events.description: the harmonic texture begins to lift, filter opens, motion increases fractionally.
events.detail: The structural turn toward the "light side": Part 16 is the hinge between the album's two halves.

events.description: the track closes on the same sparse material that opened it, but the harmonic context has shifted slightly toward resolution.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 17)
tracks.role: Album role: The light-side pivot and single — the album's most melodically direct piece; the tonal shift from the preceding three tracks is immediate and pronounced. Accompanied by a music video for its single release on 4 November 2016.

events.description: the harmonic register has shifted; the minor-mode weight of the dark side is absent.
events.detail: The tonal contrast against Parts 14–16 is the album's most structurally dramatic moment; a single heard without context misses it entirely.

events.description: the album's most immediately memorable phrase; designed for single format and broad accessibility.
distinctively modern timbre woven into the analog foundation; the only place on the album where the contemporary production is foregrounded.
events.detail: The OP-1's 4-track tape simulation and built-in synthesis give it a character recognisably different from the vintage instruments surrounding it.

events.description: brief exposure of the underlying material before the final reprise.
all elements return for the closing statement; the track ends decisively.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 18)
tracks.role: Album role: Interlude and palette cleanser — the shortest piece on the album, functioning as a meditative suspension between the single and the closing two-part finale. Its brevity is its structural function.

events.description: reduced to a single melodic line and sparse pad; no introductory build.
events.detail: At 2:48, the shortest track on the album. Its function is decompression after Part 17's melodic density.

events.section: Single melodic line over sustained pad
events.description: one voice, no counterpoint; total structural simplicity.
sequences enter briefly, suggesting the momentum of Part 19 is approaching.
the texture fragments and disappears, resolving nothing, opening everything.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 19)
tracks.role: Album role: The compositional genesis of the entire album — the piece Jarre wrote during the Electronica 1 sessions that prompted the creation of Oxygène 3. Functions as the penultimate movement, restoring momentum toward the epic finale.

events.section: Sequences recalling original Oxygène atmosphere most directly
events.description: among all the album's tracks, this most closely mirrors the feel of the 1976 original.
events.detail: Its genesis explains this: written first and independently, before the album existed, without the burden of continuation. It is the most freely composed piece here.

events.description: RMI Harmonic Synthesizer enters with its distinctive timbral colour, bridging all three albums.
events.detail: The RMI Harmonic Synthesizer appears on all three Oxygène albums; its consistent presence is one of the trilogy's sonic through-lines.

events.description: counterpoint between two sequences increases the compositional density measurably.
all elements approach maximum density before truncation; the energy does not release, it accumulates into Part 20.
atmospheric tail connects directly to the opening of Part 20.

tracks.title: Oxygène (Part 20)
tracks.role: Album role: The trilogy's concluding statement — structurally the most complex piece, opening with a direct sample of Oxygène Part VI's wind and white-noise material and building to a full-scale finale that resolves sixty-three combined minutes of sequential music across forty years. The harmonic closure of 1976 is finally completed here.

events.section: Sampled wind and white-noise from Oxygène Part VI (1976)
events.description: the opening of this track is the closing of the original album, sounded again forty years on.
events.detail: This is not homage but suture: the exact audio material of 1976 is woven into the texture of 2016, collapsing the temporal distance between the two recordings.

events.description: the sampled material begins to interact with new synthesizer voices; history and present operate simultaneously.

events.section: New material builds over historical echo
events.description: the 2016 composition asserts itself fully; the sample becomes substrate rather than subject.
the densest textural moment of the album; all instruments present, the trilogy's accumulated harmonic energy at maximum.
events.detail: The only point in Oxygène 3 that justifies comparison to the large-scale climax of Part IV on the 1976 album.

events.description: the suspended harmonics of the preceding six tracks settle at last; a landing after forty years of open cadences.
the atmospheric signature of the entire trilogy resounds one last time; the music returns to breath and air.
events.detail: The structural circle is complete: wind opened the 1976 album, wind closes the 2016 album. Three records, forty years, one atmospheric signature.
